passages.text: For I want you to know how much I am struggling for you and for those at Laodicea, and for all who have not met me face to face, that they may be encouraged in heart, knit together in love, and filled with the full riches of complete understanding, so that they may know the mystery of God, namely Christ, in whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the believers in Colossae.
Paul is also writing about the believers in Laodicea.
Paul includes all people who have not seen him in person.
Paul wants them to know something important.
Paul is struggling greatly for them.
Paul is struggling for the believers in Colossae.
Paul is struggling for the believers in Laodicea.
Paul is struggling for all who have not met him face to face.
Paul wants their hearts to be encouraged.
Paul wants them to be united in love.
Paul wants them to have complete understanding.
Paul wants them to have all the riches of full assurance and knowledge.
Paul wants them to know the mystery of God.
This mystery is Christ.
In Christ are hidden all the treasures of wisdom.
In Christ are hidden all the treasures of knowledge.
passages.original: Θέλω γὰρ ὑμᾶς εἰδέναι ἡλίκον ἀγῶνα ἔχω ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν καὶ τῶν ἐν Λαοδικείᾳ καὶ ὅσοι οὐχ ἑόρακαν τὸ πρόσωπόν μου ἐν σαρκί ἵνα παρακληθῶσιν αἱ καρδίαι αὐτῶν συμβιβασθέντες ἐν ἀγάπῃ καὶ εἰς πᾶν πλοῦτος τῆς πληροφορίας τῆς συνέσεως εἰς ἐπίγνωσιν τοῦ μυστηρίου τοῦ Θεοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐν ᾧ εἰσιν πάντες οἱ θησαυροὶ τῆς σοφίας καὶ γνώσεως ἀπόκρυφοι

passages.text: I say this so that no one will deceive you by smooth rhetoric.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the Colossians.
Paul cares deeply for them.
Paul wants to protect them.
Paul says these things for a reason.
He does not want anyone to deceive them.
He warns them about smooth and clever speech.
He wants them to stay true and not be misled.
passages.original: Τοῦτο λέγω ἵνα μηδεὶς ὑμᾶς παραλογίζηται ἐν πιθανολογίᾳ

passages.text: For although I am absent from you in body, I am present with you in spirit, and I delight to see your orderly condition and firm faith in Christ.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing this letter to the Colossians.
Paul is not with them in person.
Paul is absent from them in body.
Paul is present with them in spirit.
Paul rejoices because of them.
Paul sees their good order.
Paul sees their strong faith in Christ.
passages.original: εἰ γὰρ καὶ τῇ σαρκὶ ἄπειμι ἀλλὰ τῷ πνεύματι σὺν ὑμῖν εἰμι χαίρων καὶ βλέπων ὑμῶν τὴν τάξιν καὶ τὸ στερέωμα τῆς εἰς Χριστὸν πίστεως ὑμῶν

passages.text: Therefore, just as you have received Christ Jesus as Lord, continue to walk in Him, rooted and built up in Him, established in the faith as you were taught, and overflowing with thankfulness.
passages.sermon:
You have received Christ Jesus as Lord.
You must continue to walk in Christ.
You must be rooted in Christ.
You must be built up in Christ.
You must be established in the faith.
You were taught this faith.
You must overflow with thankfulness.
passages.original: Ὡς οὖν παρελάβετε τὸν Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν τὸν Κύριον ἐν αὐτῷ περιπατεῖτε ἐρριζωμένοι καὶ ἐποικοδομούμενοι ἐν αὐτῷ καὶ βεβαιούμενοι τῇ πίστει καθὼς ἐδιδάχθητε περισσεύοντες ἐν εὐχαριστίᾳ

passages.text: See to it that no one takes you captive through philosophy and empty deception, which are based on human tradition and the spiritual forces of the world rather than on Christ.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to Christians in Colossae.
He warns them about danger.
He says, “Be careful.”
Do not let anyone take you captive.
Some people use philosophy.
Some people use empty deception.
These teachings come from human tradition.
These teachings come from the basic principles of the world.
These teachings do not come from Christ.
passages.original: Βλέπετε μή τις ὑμᾶς ἔσται ὁ συλαγωγῶν διὰ τῆς φιλοσοφίας καὶ κενῆς ἀπάτης κατὰ τὴν παράδοσιν τῶν ἀνθρώπων κατὰ τὰ στοιχεῖα τοῦ κόσμου καὶ οὐ κατὰ Χριστόν

passages.text: For in Christ all the fullness of the Deity dwells in bodily form.
passages.sermon:
Christ is a person.
Christ is God.
God’s complete nature lives in Christ.
God’s fullness is present in Christ’s body.
God lives in Christ in a real, physical way.
passages.original: ὅτι ἐν αὐτῷ κατοικεῖ πᾶν τὸ πλήρωμα τῆς Θεότητος σωματικῶς

passages.text: And you have been made complete in Christ, who is the head over every ruler and authority.
passages.sermon: Christ is the head over every ruler and authority.\r\nYou are in Christ.\r\nGod has made you complete in Christ.
passages.original: καὶ ἐστὲ ἐν αὐτῷ πεπληρωμένοι ὅς ἐστιν ἡ κεφαλὴ πάσης ἀρχῆς καὶ ἐξουσίας

passages.text: In Him you were also circumcised, in the putting off of your sinful nature, with the circumcision performed by Christ and not by human hands.
passages.sermon:
Christ is the one in whom all the fullness of God lives in bodily form.
Christ is the head over every ruler and authority.
You are in Christ.
Christ performed a circumcision on you.
This circumcision was not done by human hands.
This circumcision removed your sinful nature.
Christ Himself did this for you.
passages.original: ἐν ᾧ καὶ περιετμήθητε περιτομῇ ἀχειροποιήτῳ ἐν τῇ ἀπεκδύσει τοῦ σώματος τῆς σαρκός ἐν τῇ περιτομῇ τοῦ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: And having been buried with Him in baptism, you were raised with Him through your faith in the power of God, who raised Him from the dead.
passages.sermon:
You are united with Christ.
You were buried with Christ in baptism.
God raised Christ from the dead.
You were also raised with Christ.
God did this through His power.
You received this by faith in God.
passages.original: συνταφέντες αὐτῷ ἐν τῷ βαπτισμῷ ἐν ᾧ καὶ συνηγέρθητε διὰ τῆς πίστεως τῆς ἐνεργείας τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦ ἐγείραντος αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν

passages.text: When you were dead in your trespasses and in the uncircumcision of your sinful nature, God made you alive with Christ. He forgave us all our trespasses, having canceled the debt ascribed to us in the decrees that stood against us. He took it away, nailing it to the cross!
passages.sermon:
God acted when you were dead in your sins.
You were dead because of your trespasses.
You were also dead because your sinful nature was uncircumcised.
God made you alive together with Christ.
God forgave us all our trespasses.
God canceled the written record of debt that stood against us.
This record was set out in the decrees that opposed us.
God took this record away.
God nailed it to the cross.
passages.original: Καὶ ὑμᾶς νεκροὺς ὄντας ἐν τοῖς παραπτώμασιν καὶ τῇ ἀκροβυστίᾳ τῆς σαρκὸς ὑμῶν συνεζωοποίησεν ὑμᾶς σὺν αὐτῷ χαρισάμενος ἡμῖν πάντα τὰ παραπτώματα ἐξαλείψας τὸ καθ’ ἡμῶν χειρόγραφον τοῖς δόγμασιν ὃ ἦν ὑπεναντίον ἡμῖν καὶ αὐτὸ ἦρκεν ἐκ τοῦ μέσου προσηλώσας αὐτὸ τῷ σταυρῷ

passages.text: And having disarmed the powers and authorities, He made a public spectacle of them, triumphing over them by the cross.
passages.sermon: Jesus Christ disarmed the powers and authorities.\r\nHe made a public spectacle of these powers and authorities.\r\nHe triumphed over them by the cross.
passages.original: ἀπεκδυσάμενος τὰς ἀρχὰς καὶ τὰς ἐξουσίας ἐδειγμάτισεν ἐν παρρησίᾳ θριαμβεύσας αὐτοὺς ἐν αὐτῷ

passages.text: Therefore let no one judge you by what you eat or drink, or with regard to a feast, a New Moon, or a Sabbath.
passages.sermon:
God made you alive with Christ.
God forgave all your trespasses.
God canceled the debt that stood against you.
God took away the record of your sins.
God nailed it to the cross.
Therefore, do not let anyone judge you.
Do not let anyone judge you by what you eat.
Do not let anyone judge you by what you drink.
Do not let anyone judge you about a feast.
Do not let anyone judge you about a New Moon.
Do not let anyone judge you about a Sabbath.
passages.original: Μὴ οὖν τις ὑμᾶς κρινέτω ἐν βρώσει καὶ ἐν πόσει ἢ ἐν μέρει ἑορτῆς ἢ νεομηνίας ἢ σαββάτων

passages.text: These are a shadow of the things to come, but the body that casts it belongs to Christ.
passages.sermon: These things are only a shadow of what is coming.\r\nThe reality belongs to Christ.\r\nChrist is the one who fulfills what these things point to.
passages.original: ἅ ἐστιν σκιὰ τῶν μελλόντων τὸ δὲ σῶμα τοῦ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: Do not let anyone who delights in false humility and the worship of angels disqualify you with speculation about what he has seen. Such a person is puffed up without basis by his unspiritual mind.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote to the Colossians.
Paul warned them about false teachers.
Some people pretend to be humble.
Some people worship angels.
Some people claim to have special visions.
Do not let these people disqualify you.
They use their own ideas to judge you.
They are proud without reason.
Their minds are not spiritual.
They are not connected to Christ.
passages.original: μηδεὶς ὑμᾶς καταβραβευέτω θέλων ἐν ταπεινοφροσύνῃ καὶ θρησκείᾳ τῶν ἀγγέλων ἃ ἑόρακεν ἐμβατεύων εἰκῇ φυσιούμενος ὑπὸ τοῦ νοὸς τῆς σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ

passages.text: He has lost connection to the head, from whom the whole body, supported and knit together by its joints and ligaments, grows as God causes it to grow.
passages.sermon:
This person has lost connection to the head.
The head is Christ.
The whole body depends on Christ.
The body receives support from its joints and ligaments.
The body is held together by these parts.
God causes the body to grow.
The body grows as God gives it growth.
passages.original: καὶ οὐ κρατῶν τὴν Κεφαλήν ἐξ οὗ πᾶν τὸ σῶμα διὰ τῶν ἁφῶν καὶ συνδέσμων ἐπιχορηγούμενον καὶ συμβιβαζόμενον αὔξει τὴν αὔξησιν τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: If you have died with Christ to the spiritual forces of the world, why, as though you still belonged to the world, do you submit to its regulations: “Do not handle, do not taste, do not touch!”?
passages.sermon:
You have died with Christ.
You have died to the spiritual forces of the world.
You do not belong to the world anymore.
Why do you act as if you still live in the world?
Why do you submit to its rules?
These rules say, “Do not handle.”
They say, “Do not taste.”
They say, “Do not touch.”
passages.original: Εἰ ἀπεθάνετε σὺν Χριστῷ ἀπὸ τῶν στοιχείων τοῦ κόσμου τί ὡς ζῶντες ἐν κόσμῳ δογματίζεσθε Μὴ ἅψῃ μηδὲ γεύσῃ μηδὲ θίγῃς

passages.text: These will all perish with use, because they are based on human commands and teachings.
passages.sermon: These things will all perish when people use them.\r\nThey are based on human commands.\r\nThey are based on human teachings.
passages.original: ἅ ἐστιν πάντα εἰς φθορὰν τῇ ἀποχρήσει κατὰ τὰ ἐντάλματα καὶ διδασκαλίας τῶν ἀνθρώπων

passages.text: Such restrictions indeed have an appearance of wisdom, with their self-prescribed worship, their false humility, and their harsh treatment of the body; but they are of no value against the indulgence of the flesh.
passages.sermon:
These rules look wise.
They seem wise because people invent their own ways to worship.
They seem wise because people act humble.
They seem wise because people treat their bodies harshly.
These rules do not really help.
These rules cannot stop people from following their sinful desires.
passages.original: ἅτινά ἐστιν λόγον μὲν ἔχοντα σοφίας ἐν ἐθελοθρησκίᾳ καὶ ταπεινοφροσύνῃ καὶ ἀφειδίᾳ σώματος οὐκ ἐν τιμῇ τινι πρὸς πλησμονὴν τῆς σαρκός
